title: CtlError
description:
The shape of EVERY non-2xx body the control plane emits, including the 404 for an unknown route and the 429 from the rate limiter. Unlike the tenant API's `error.json` (which models what FastAPI already shipped), this one is contract-first for a new Go daemon, so it can require the machine-readable `code` and the correlation `request_id` from the start.

`code` is the field a client branches on; `detail` is server prose for operators and logs (it may name paths, units and hosts — the admin UI never renders it verbatim). `extra` carries the typed payload some codes need: `confirm_required` puts the expected `confirm` value there, `plan_stale` the current `plan_hash` and `registry_generation`, `locked` the holder `{job_id, since}`, `duplicate` the original `job_id`, `doctor_red` the `doctor_hash`, `rate_limited` the `retry_after` seconds.

Status mapping (one status per code, so the code alone is enough to reconstruct the status in a log): `both_credentials` 400 · `auth_required` 401 · `forbidden` 403 · `not_found` 404 (also the 410 of an already-delivered secrets envelope, whose body says so in `detail`) · `locked` / `plan_stale` / `duplicate` / `doctor_red` / `refused` 409 · `validation` 422 · `confirm_required` 428 · `rate_limited` 429 · `internal` 500.

detail.description: What went wrong, as a human-readable sentence. Always a string here — the Go daemon owns its validation body, so there is no FastAPI-style list variant; per-field validation problems go under `extra.fields`.

code.description: Machine-readable failure class. `auth_required`: no usable credential (absent, malformed, unknown key, bad signature, expired token, revoked session). `forbidden`: the credential verified but the subject is not on the ctl's principal list, or its role is below the operation's minimum — there is NEVER a default role. `both_credentials`: `X-API-Key` and `Authorization` on one request (or a body `ctl_api_key` that differs from the header key). `refused`: a policy or precondition refusal that is not a lock/plan/doctor/confirm problem — a store with `capabilities.<x>: false`, an unfenced backup offered where a fenced one is required, a containment or ownership check, an executable-surface key on the HTTP settings path.

request_id.description: The correlation id for the failed request — identical to the `X-Request-Id` response header and to the `rid=` on every log line and audit row the request produced. Redundant with the header on purpose: a header does not survive a user pasting the body into a ticket.

extra.description: Code-specific typed payload; absent when the code needs none. Free-form by necessity (each code has its own shape, documented on `code`), but it is the ONLY untyped member and it never carries a secret value.
